absent: Exact memory layouts and field offsets for lock classes, held locks, chains, traces, and adjacency nodes.
Chain key mixing function, seed value, hash table sizing, and hash collision probability handling beyond alias detection.
Breadth search implementation, queue capacity constant, traversal order, and detailed error conditions.
Graph lock type, acquisition ordering, and interrupt masking implementation beyond the locked with interrupts disabled assertion.
Interrupt usage predicates, usage mask bit assignments, and trace retention rules.
Stack trace capture implementation and lifetime management.
Class comparator and nesting serialiser contracts beyond ordering exemption and nesting suppression.
Configuration conditions selecting between redundant check variants and chain validation variants.
Counter widths, overflow behaviour, and concurrency protection for chain statistics.
Adjacency distance and dependency bit encodings beyond direct adjacency marking and monotonic strengthening.
Diagnostic output formatting and console guard implementation details.
Chain reclamation, zapping, and loss accounting triggers.

findings.text: The dossier provides public iteration over cached lock chains together with a population count. Iteration moves a supplied position forward to the next slot marked in use and signals exhaustion with a dedicated negative value. Counting reports the number of slots currently marked in use.

The dossier provides public translation from a logical position within a cached chain to the associated class descriptor. The operation reads the compact identifier held for that position and resolves it through the global class table.

Validation of a newly observed acquisition acts as the main gate for dependency learning. When the acquisition is eligible and its key is novel, deadlock and predecessor checks run while the graph is held. Try acquisitions, unchecked acquisitions, and already cached keys bypass learning while still respecting the global disable flag. One configuration always reports success without performing work.

Predecessor linkage walks the current held stack backward from the top within a single interrupt context. Each checked entry is validated against the incoming acquisition, traversal halts once an ordinary non try acquisition has been processed, and empty depth or context mismatch is treated as a state error that disables graph tracking and warns.

Dependency search equality requires the same class on both sides plus compatible access mode marking. A read style acquisition matches any stored marking, while other acquisitions match only when the stored entry is not marked as exclusive only.

Redundancy detection searches for an existing path of sufficient strength relative to the candidate edge. The search start is seeded according to the source access mode so that exclusive sources seek only exclusive led paths while shared sources accept either strength, and a particular lightweight lock family is skipped because paths through it are not equivalent. One configuration counts attempts and matches, while an alternate configuration always reports no match.

Cached chain population is accounted per execution context with mutually exclusive classification. Hard interrupt context takes precedence over soft interrupt context, and anything else counts as process context, with symmetric increment and decrement operations.

Deadlock checking scans the current held stack for an earlier acquisition of the same class as the incoming one. Repeated shared style reuse is permitted, strictly increasing instance order under an optional class comparator is exempt, and holding the designated nesting serialiser suppresses the report with a distinct outcome. Otherwise a same class re acquisition is reported as a deadlock.

Adding a predecessor edge performs liveness, ordering, circularity, interrupt usage, duplication, and redundancy checks before insertion. Existing edges are strengthened in both forward and backward adjacency with direct adjacency remembered, redundant edges are dropped without insertion, and fresh edges capture a stack trace once and insert symmetric forward and backward links.

Variable length identifier blocks are carved from a shared compact array using a bucketed free list. Free blocks carry a marker in a high bit and encode their successor across paired entries, allocation prefers an exact size bucket then the variable bucket with splitting of remainders and finally larger buckets, requests below two units are raised to two, and release returns the range to the free lists.

Chain cache insertion records the current contiguous interrupt context slice together with the incoming acquisition under a supplied key. It allocates a chain descriptor and identifier storage, copies the slice and the new entry, links the chain into a hash table, and updates miss and per context counts. Exhaustion of either table disables tracking with diagnostics.

Cache lookup and insertion uses an unlocked fast probe followed by a locked re probe to prevent duplicate entries. A hit verifies absence of key aliasing and may log verbosely, while a miss inserts under the graph lock. Hit and miss paths return distinct outcomes that tell the caller whether dependency learning is required.

A debug only self check rebuilds expected chain keys by walking the held stack from the bottom, resetting the accumulator whenever interrupt context changes and confirming that each class index is registered. Any divergence from stored predecessor keys or the current key disables tracking and warns, indicating corrupted task state.

Usage validation refuses an acquisition whose class already carries a forbidden prior usage marking. The refusal releases the graph before emitting the inconsistency report, while the allowed case simply continues with the graph still held.

Mutation of the dependency graph and chain cache requires holding the global graph lock with interrupts disabled. The lock is acquired for insertion after the unlocked probe, held across deadlock and predecessor validation for novel keys, and released before usage inconsistency reporting and on error paths that disable tracking.

Collision and usage diagnostics run under a console emergency guard that is entered before warning output and stack capture and exited afterwards, isolating the report from concurrent console activity.

Cached chains live in a fixed size table whose capacity is governed by a maximum chains limit. Each slot holds key, context, depth, base offset, and hash linkage, with a parallel bitmap recording which slots are in use.

Chain member identifiers live in a shared fixed size array of narrow units together with separate accounting for reclaimed chains, free units, lost units, and oversized blocks. Allocation failures and reclamation update these counters rather than moving stored chains.

Free block lookup uses a small fixed size directory indexed by size class, with one entry reserved for variable sized large blocks kept in size order. Each entry holds the head offset of its free list or a negative value when empty.

Deadlock evaluation reports three distinct outcomes. One outcome signals a detected deadlock after emitting a report, a second signals safety to proceed, and a third signals that nesting is serialised by a held outer lock so dependency learning should be skipped.

Predecessor edge evaluation reports three distinct outcomes. Failure covers circularity, interrupt misuse, allocation failure, and inconsistent adjacency. Already present covers strengthening of an existing edge. The remaining outcome covers newly inserted edges, redundant edges, and skipped ordered or keyless cases.

Cache and validation evaluation distinguishes novel keys from already cached or failed cases. Novel insertion requests dependency learning under the graph lock, while cache hits and ineligible acquisitions skip learning. A disabled global flag forces failure after lookup.

Exhaustion of the chain table or the identifier store is a tracking hazard that permanently disables dependency checking for the session. The implementation emits a dedicated capacity diagnostic with a stack capture while forgetting the current insertion.

Key aliasing, missing class keys, asymmetric adjacency, and key reconstruction divergence all indicate corruption or unsafe reuse. Aliasing triggers a collision report comparing held and cached contents, missing keys trigger lifetime warnings suggesting freed class memory, asymmetric adjacency fails validation, and reconstruction divergence warns about corrupted task state.
The size class directory contains sixteen entries.
Free list membership is marked by a single flag bit at position fifteen of a narrow storage unit, and the free list terminator is the value with all sixteen bits set.

Diagnostic helpers expand chain keys step by step while naming each member, contrast the current held stack against a cached chain on aliasing, and sketch a two level interrupt nesting scenario to illustrate unsafe reuse. These helpers only format information for reports and do not affect tracking state.
